title: Impedance Triangle: R + jX as One Phasor
topic: AC impedance for a series R-L-C — resistors carry pure R, inductors give +jωL, capacitors give −j/(ωC). Stack them on the complex plane and the net impedance Z = R + jX is one phasor with magnitude √(R² + X²) and angle arctan(X/R). Sweep ω and Z rotates from capacitive (below the axis) through resonance (on the axis) to inductive (above).

beats.narration: Resistors live on the real axis. Inductors and capacitors live on the imaginary axis. So how does a series R L C even have one impedance?

elements.content: Manimo bobs in centre-screen
Stack R, jωL and −j/ωC — and Z drops out as one phasor.

beats.narration: Three elements in series. The resistor has impedance R, a real number. The inductor adds j times omega L — purely imaginary, pointing up. The capacitor adds minus j over omega C — also imaginary, pointing down.

elements.content: Series R-L-C circuit drawn on the left
Z_R = R label next to resistor (real axis)
Z_L = jωL label next to inductor (imaginary, +up)
Z_C = −j/(ωC) label next to capacitor (imaginary, −down)
real for the resistor, imaginary for L and C

beats.narration: Plot them on the complex plane. R is the horizontal leg. Stack the inductive arrow up and the capacitive arrow down — their difference is the net reactance X. The hypotenuse from origin to the tip is the total impedance Z, with magnitude root R squared plus X squared and angle arctan X over R.

elements.content: Complex plane with real (Re) and imaginary (Im) axes labelled
Horizontal arrow of length R along +Re (amber)
Vertical arrow of length jωL upward stacked at the R-tip (teal)
Vertical arrow of length 1/(ωC) downward stacked at top of the jωL arrow (rose)
Net reactance X = ωL − 1/(ωC) annotated on the y-leg
Z phasor — hypotenuse from origin to the stacked tip, with magnitude and angle labelled (genuine motion: it draws in)
|Z| = √(R² + X²)   tan(φ) = X/R

beats.narration: Now sweep omega from low to high. At low frequency the capacitor's huge impedance dominates, so X is negative and Z dips below the real axis — the circuit looks capacitive. Push omega up and the two reactances cross at resonance, where X equals zero and Z lies flat on the real axis. Above resonance the inductor wins, X goes positive, and Z swings up — the circuit looks inductive.

elements.content: Same complex plane axes from previous beat
Z phasor live-rotating as omega sweeps — tip traces the vertical line x=R as X changes from negative to positive (genuine value-driven motion)
Live omega readout + phase angle φ readout updating each frame
Region badges: CAPACITIVE, RESONANT, INDUCTIVE — light up as Z passes them

beats.narration: Impedance is one complex number — real part the resistor, imaginary part the reactance. Magnitude tells you the size, angle tells you the phase between voltage and current.

elements.content: Z = R + jX — one phasor, two truths about an AC circuit.
|Z| sets the current. arg(Z) sets the lag.
